**Still broken on v2.0.5** — reproduced live (Linux, background subagents enabled). Fix #49305 is unmerged (`BLOCKED`) and the binary lacks its symbols.

Timeline (t=0 = spawn; child starts a `sleep 20` background shell, then ends its turn early):
- +3s — child idle `succeeded`, shell still running
- +16s — parent gets the **only** notification: `completed` + early reply, **6s before the shell finished**
- +22s — shell completes; child is woken and produces its real result
- parent **never** receives it — nothing pending, result stranded in the child session

Nuance: the wake *did* reach the child here; the parent-side delivery failure is what reproduces. An isolated `opencode run --standalone` trial also showed the early notification, and there the pending shell never completed (likely killed at run exit) — possible extra severity variant.

Hit this on a plain desktop OpenCode session (1.18.31, Windows), not headless/systemd — worth noting since it rules out multi-tenant/systemd specifics as the trigger.

My case matches your "a freshly created session's first batch was already collapsed" note exactly — mine fails on the very first tool-using turn of a brand new session, not after a batch that previously worked.

Setup: `provider.anthropic.options.baseURL` pointed at a custom Anthropic-compatible gateway (not api.anthropic.com). Plain chat through it works fine.

What I confirmed:
- Ran a local logging proxy in place of my real backend and captured the actual request OpenCode sends. The `tools` array is present and correct every time — 11 real tools (`bash`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `question`, `read`, `skill`, `task`, `todowrite`, `webfetch`, `write`) plus `tool_choice`. So it's leaving the client fine.
- Checked `opencode.log` for the failing turn: no tool-call round-trip logged at all, just one `stream` call and straight to `exiting loop`. The model never actually attempted a call the harness could see.
- The model then writes a confident explanation instead — "I attempted the write tool and the bash tool again, both calls failed with Error: No such tool available" — and even lists which tools *were* "available," a list that doesn't match what was actually sent in the request.
- Reproduced identically against two independent backend instances behind the same gateway software — same result on both, so it's not one flaky backend on my end.

Consistent with your theory: the live registry look-up is disposed/empty at request-build time, but the prompt still names the tools, so the model has nothing real to call but still "knows" tool names exist — and fills the gap with a plausible but fabricated explanation instead of a visible error.

**Follow-up and correction to my comment above — I found the root cause, and it is not opencode.**

I previously guessed the delay might be the same family as the `input.focused` guard in #48607. That was wrong. Same opencode2 build, same session, same terminal — only one thing changed:

**Environment**
- opencode2 `v2.0.3`
- macOS 27.0 (build 26A428), arm64
- Ghostty
- zsh with `microsoft/inshellisense` `0.0.4` (Homebrew) sourced from `.zshrc`

**Behavior**
- With inshellisense loaded: pressing `Esc` **does** register, but it takes roughly **1–2 s** before the running turn actually stops, so the interrupt feels unresponsive / laggy.
- With the inshellisense init line commented out in `.zshrc`: `Esc` interrupts **instantly** — same build, same session, same terminal, nothing else changed.

The line in question:

```zsh
# [[ -f "$HOME/.local/share/inshellisense/init/zsh/init.zsh" ]] && source "$HOME/.local/share/inshellisense/init/zsh/init.zsh"
```

So the latency is introduced by the shell-level key interceptor that wraps the terminal, not by opencode's interrupt path. That is also why removing the focus guard in #48607 does not address this particular delay: the key is not being dropped, it is being delayed before opencode ever sees it.

If anyone else finds `Esc` (or keys in general) sluggish in the TUI, please rule this out first: check whether a shell wrapper such as inshellisense — or another zsh autocomplete plugin that owns keybindings — is active, and try disabling it before digging into the TUI.

inshellisense has related precedent for TUI conflicts: microsoft/inshellisense#411 (lazygit/lazydocker layout broken inside an `is` session) and microsoft/inshellisense#418 (Up/Down arrows stolen from shell history). I have filed the TUI-latency report there as well: microsoft/inshellisense#480.

Maintainers: a one-line Troubleshooting entry ("if Esc/keys feel laggy, rule out shell wrappers like inshellisense") would likely save other users this exact rabbit hole.

Correction to my earlier comment — the root cause in my case was **my gateway, not OpenCode**. OpenCode was behaving correctly the whole time; I want to set the record straight so nobody chases a phantom registry bug on the strength of my report.

What was actually happening behind that custom `baseURL`: my gateway wraps a CLI that exposes function-calling to clients via a prompt protocol (tool schemas injected into the system prompt; the model is asked to reply with a `{"tool_calls":[...]}` envelope, which the gateway converts back into Anthropic `tool_use` blocks). The bug was entirely on my side: the underlying agent's own built-in tools — including a `ToolSearch`-style tool-discovery tool — were never disabled. So when OpenCode's request told the model to call `write`/`bash`, the model tried to *load* those as native tools via tool-discovery instead of emitting the envelope, and emitted bare argument objects (`{"filePath":...}`) with no tool name. My parser couldn't recognize a nameless blob, so it streamed as plain text — and once that landed in the transcript, later turns spiraled into exactly the fabricated "No such tool available" explanation I quoted.

That also explains the two things that looked like OpenCode bugs but weren't:
- The `tools` array leaving the client "correct every time" — because it was. The failure was downstream, in how my gateway relayed the model's reply.
- The model "listing tools that don't match what was sent" — those were the gateway's own undisabled built-ins leaking through, not OpenCode's registry.

Fix was on my end: deny the agent's discovery/orchestration built-ins so the only path to a tool call is the envelope. After that, a real OpenCode request (185KB system, 11 tools) produces a clean `write` tool_use block with `stop_reason: tool_use` and zero leaked text, first turn.

Apologies for the noise — please disregard my report as evidence for a registry-divergence issue in OpenCode.

Root cause found for this generic 400, at least for `muse-spark-*` on OpenCode Go / Zen.

The Console gateways **advertise `max` as a supported reasoning effort but reject it upstream** with exactly the generic message from this issue.

Minimal repro against `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses` (no tools, no history, one message):

```bash
curl https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"muse-spark-1.3-contributor","input":[{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"input_text","text":"hi"}]}],"max_output_tokens":16,"reasoning":{"effort":"max"}}'
```

Observed results:

| `reasoning.effort` | result |
|---|---|
| omitted | 200 |
| `minimal` (checked via `none` error listing) | supported |
| `high` | 200 |
| `xhigh` | 200 |
| `max` | **400** generic `invalid_request_error` (see below) |
| `none` | 400 `reasoning_effort 'none' is not supported for model 'muse-spark-1.3-contributor'. Supported values: [minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max]` |

`effort: "max"` returns exactly the message from this issue:

```json
{"model":"muse-spark-1.3-contributor","error":{"param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] The request contains invalid parameters. Check the request body for any errors or inconsistencies."}}
```

So the validator lists `max` as supported but the request is still rejected — looks like a gateway/upstream bug on the top tier.

Why OpenCode users hit this: agent-level `options.reasoningEffort` is forwarded to whatever model is selected, so any agent that pins `reasoningEffort: "max"` (typically for another model) makes every `muse-spark-*` request fail on turn 1. Reproduced end-to-end on 1.18.31:

- default `build` agent (`options.reasoningEffort: max`) + `-m opencode-go/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` → same 400 on the first message
- same run with `--variant xhigh` → succeeds
- same run with a dedicated agent using `options.reasoningEffort: "xhigh"` → succeeds

Workaround until fixed: for Muse Spark, use variant `xhigh` (or an agent configured with `high`/`xhigh`); never send `effort: max` to these models.
thank you!

Experiencing the same class of bug on **v1.18.31**, but with a different `finish_reason` value. Filing here instead of opening a duplicate because the underlying issue (opencode trusts provider's `finish_reason` and loops when it's wrong) is identical.

**Setup**
- Provider: custom gateway proxying GLM-5.2, configured with `npm: "@ai-sdk/anthropic"`
- Trigger: any user message (even just "你好")

**What happens**
The agent loop never terminates. First ESC aborts the current stream; the loop immediately restarts from `step=0`. Second ESC finally kills it.

**Hard evidence** (queried from `opencode.db`, session with ~360 assistant turns in one exchange):

| `finish` | count | sum(`tokens.output`) |
|---|---|---|
| `unknown` | 331 | **0** |
| `tool-calls` | 10 | 3189 |
| `""` | 11 | 0 |

Sample assistant message record:

```json
{
  "role": "assistant",
  "agent": "Sisyphus - Ultraworker",
  "cost": 0,
  "tokens": {"input":0,"output":0,"reasoning":0,"cache":{"write":0,"read":0}},
  "modelID": "glm-5.2",
  "providerID": "tal",
  "time": {"created": 1789631840516, "completed": 1789631844256},
  "finish": "unknown"
}
```

**How this variant differs from the reporter's case**
- Reporter's case: provider returns `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` for plain text → opencode expects tool calls, finds none, continues.
- My case: provider returns `finish_reason: "unknown"` (or the Anthropic SDK fails to parse a missing/empty `stop_reason`) with **zero output tokens** → opencode doesn't see a terminal state and continues.

Both are "opencode re-invokes because `finish_reason` doesn't signal end-of-turn" — just with different invalid values.

**Guard suggestion**
The proposed fix for this issue (stop when `tool_calls` is set but no calls are present) should be broadened to also treat `finish === "unknown"` **combined with `tokens.output === 0`** as a terminal state. In this case the provider produced no content, so continuing has no useful purpose — the loop can only ever burn more tokens with no output.

**Tried and did not work**
- `agent.sisyphus.steps: 1` — ignored, session still ran ~30 steps before first ESC.
- `provider.tal.options.chunkTimeout: 5000` — did not fire; SSE chunks keep arriving with empty content.

Follow-up / correction to my previous comment — I called it fixed too early. The first change (disabling the agent's discovery/orchestration built-ins) removed the raw-JSON leak but did **not** reliably make tool calls work: a fresh OpenCode session still narrated "the write/bash tools are disabled" and made no call, roughly 7 times out of 8. One lucky pass isn't a fix.

The actual root cause, confirmed by tapping the underlying CLI's event stream for a real OpenCode request:

My gateway still left the model **two real native tools** on (its web fetch/search pair). That kept the model in native tool-calling mode. Under OpenCode's large agent system prompt — which frames `write`/`bash` as native tools — the model emitted native `tool_use` blocks named after **OpenCode's** tools, which the CLI rejected (it has no such tools), instead of the `{"tool_calls":...}` text envelope my gateway relays. When those native calls failed, the model concluded the tools were "disabled" and gave up.

Fix on my end: when a request carries its own tools, offer the CLI **zero** native tools. With no native tools there is no `tool_use` grammar available at all, so plain text — and therefore the envelope — is the only output channel. The model complies every time.

Verified end to end: a fresh OpenCode session created and ran a file on disk (`fibonacci(10)` → 55), with write and bash executing for real, 3/3 on repeat.

Net: still entirely a bug on my gateway side, not OpenCode. Two separate mistakes on my part were needed to produce the symptom (undisabled discovery tools + a non-empty native toolset), which is why my earlier "fixed" was premature. Sorry for the back-and-forth — please continue to disregard this as evidence of an OpenCode registry issue.

Thanks @LouisLau-art for isolating the `User-Agent` check. I hit the same error from a different client and reproduced it on purpose. This adds a second, independent condition the gate enforces.

### Context

`pi` is a coding agent with a built-in `opencode` provider. It sends `x-opencode-client: pi` for attribution. Since 2026-09-17 the free tier returns for every free model:

```
OpenAI API error (403): {"type":"FreeTierError","message":"Error from provider (Console): OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"}
```

The error appears on two hosts (macOS and Windows), with the same key and the same `pi` version, and without the OpenCode CLI involved. That is why I looked at the request fingerprint rather than at the account.

### Method

I sent direct requests to `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/responses` with `Authorization: Bearer public` (anonymous free tier) and a minimal JSON body, then varied one header at a time.

### Finding 1 — `User-Agent` must be `opencode/<recent semver>`

| `User-Agent` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `opencode/1.18.31` | 200 |
| `opencode/latest/1.18.31/cli` | 200 |
| `opencode/999.0.0` | 200 |
| `OpenCode/1.18.31` | 200 |
| `opencode/0.0.0` | 426 |
| `opencode/latest` | 403 |
| `opencode/` | 403 |
| `opencode` (no slash) | 403 |
| `pi (darwin 25.6.0; arm64)` | 403 |
| `curl/8.7.1` | 403 |
| `OpenAI/JS 6.40.0` | 403 |
| header absent | 403 |

This matches #49430/#49431 (`1.17.0 or newer is required`) and the git-describe rejection. The trailing SDK tags (`ai-sdk/provider-utils/... runtime/bun/...`) are not required: plain `opencode/1.18.31` passes, and `OpenCode/1.18.31` passes, so the match is case-insensitive.

### Finding 2 — `x-opencode-session` must be an OpenCode session ID

With `User-Agent: opencode/1.18.31` fixed, the session header is a second independent gate. The accepted format is `ses_` + 12 hex characters + 14 base62 characters, i.e. what `Identifier.create` produces in `packages/opencode/src/id/id.ts`.

| `x-opencode-session` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `ses_<12 hex><14 base62>` | 200 |
| `ses_` + 12 hex time + `AAAAAAAAAAAAAA` | 403 |
| `ses_AAAAAAAAAAAA` + 14 random base62 | 403 |
| `<uuid>` (e.g. `01a0af13-c6df-73c6-8803-9e6d9c720da7`) | 403 |
| same value without the `ses_` prefix | 403 |
| empty string | 403 |
| header absent | 403 |

Notes from the same tests:

- The 12-hex time component is not checked for recency. Timestamps from now back to one year ago pass; an all-`A` component (which decodes to ~1971) fails. So the gate looks for a plausible timestamp, not an exact one.
- `x-opencode-client` is not validated. `cli` and `pi` both pass with a valid session.
- `x-opencode-request` and `x-opencode-project` are not required.
- The body is irrelevant: a full agent payload and a minimal `{"model","input","stream"}` payload behave the same.
- The gate is not key-based: `Bearer public` and a real account key both pass with a valid fingerprint.

So a request to the free tier needs **both** an `opencode/`-style `User-Agent` **and** a `ses_`-formatted session ID. A third-party client that reports an honest `User-Agent` (as `pi` does) is rejected twice: once on the UA and once on its own UUID session.

### Request

Could the OpenCode team make the free-tier client requirements explicit in the docs? Concretely:

1. Is the free tier intended to be limited to the official OpenCode client? If known third-party clients are supported, what should they send? `pi` already sends `x-opencode-client: pi`, which suggests third-party attribution was intended.
2. Can you document the accepted `User-Agent` form and the required `x-opencode-session` format in one place, so client authors can comply instead of reverse-engineering the edge service? A `1.17.0 or newer` minimum and a session-ID requirement would be enough.
